title: Basic English — Course 2, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 2

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Where will the workshop take place?
tasks.audioText: The college library is holding a workshop on checking information found online. It will take place in the digital study room on Tuesday at two. Students will practise checking the author, publication date and supporting evidence. They should bring a laptop if they have one, but a limited number of college devices will be available to borrow.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. What will students practise checking?
tasks.audioText: The college library is holding a workshop on checking information found online. It will take place in the digital study room on Tuesday at two. Students will practise checking the author, publication date and supporting evidence. They should bring a laptop if they have one, but a limited number of college devices will be available to borrow.
options: The equipment serial number and model
The author, publication date and supporting evidence
The room booking and lesson timetable

tasks.prompt: When a student researched renewable energy, the first website she found made a strong claim but did not identify its author or provide links to evidence. She compared the information with a government report and a university article. The sources agreed on the general trend but used different figures because they covered different years. She included the dates and explained the difference in her assignment. Reading 1. Why did the student question the first website?
options: It was published too recently to assess
It had no named author or supporting evidence
It disagreed with every other source

tasks.prompt: Why were the figures different in the other sources?
options: They were collected by different research teams

tasks.prompt: The report ___ by a university research team last year.
Choose TWO checks that help evaluate an online source.
options: Trust it because the headline is dramatic

tasks.prompt: Information that supports a statement or conclusion is ___.
You need to explain why you used a source. Which sentence is suitable?
options: I copied it because the title looked interesting.
I used this source because it provides recent data and identifies its research method.
I did not check where the information came from.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of online information in a logical order.
options: Compare the claim with reliable evidence
Identify the claim you need to check
Explain your conclusion and cite the sources
Find the author and publication date
correctOrder: Identify the claim you need to check
Find the author and publication date
Compare the claim with reliable evidence
Explain your conclusion and cite the sources

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how students can decide whether an online source is reliable. Include at least three checks.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: at least three distinct reliability checks are explained (0–2); checks address relevant factors such as author/organisation, date, evidence/references and confirmation from another reliable source (0–2); advice is logically connected with understandable grammar (0–2); source-evaluation vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are appropriate (0–2).
